The higher-authority business evidence—the quantitative segment analysis, the CEO’s strategic directive, and the founding mission—supports prioritizing regulated mid-market and enterprise organizations, not education startups or SMBs. While the sales playbook previously highlighted education startups [NL-016#NL-016-S03] and sales leadership argued for doubling down on them [NL-015#NL-015-S03], the data refutes that: mid-market (28 accounts) and enterprise (9 accounts) together generate 83.8% of recurring revenue [NL-016#NL-016-S03], with lower monthly logo churn (enterprise 1.3%, mid-market 2.1% vs SMB 4.8%) and higher NPS (enterprise 52, mid-market 47 vs SMB 31) [NL-016#NL-016-S03][NL-015#NL-015-S03]. The CEO explicitly states the ICP is regulated mid-market and enterprise organizations [NL-015#NL-015-S03], and the company mission confirms it has grown by targeting mid-market and enterprise accounts requiring rigorous governance [NL-001#NL-001-S02]. The sales team’s emphasis on education startups is therefore contradicted by the measured long-term value of regulated accounts [NL-016#NL-016-S03].

The trade-off that comes with this segment priority is a longer and more complex sales and onboarding cycle. Enterprise onboarding takes a median of 8.7 weeks due to permission and security complexities, while mid-market averages 5.2 weeks [NL-016#NL-016-S03][NL-015#NL-015-S03]. In contrast, the SMB path of least resistance closes in under 3 weeks with credit-card payment and minimal security reviews [NL-015#NL-015-S03]. This slower, more demanding cycle requires sales teams to navigate security reviews and permission mapping, rather than chasing quick SMB wins [NL-015#NL-015-S03].
